body.p: This application has been carefully reviewed in light of the Office Action mailed August 19, 2024. At the time of the Office Action, claims 1-27 were pending, of which, claims 1-11 are rejected and claims 12-27 are allowed. With this amendment, Applicant has amended claims 1, 3, 4, and 8. No new matter has been introduced. Reconsideration of the above-identified application in view of the present amendments and the following remarks is respectfully requested.

Claims 1-11 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(a) as failing to comply with the enablement requirement. According to the Office Action, there is no original disclosure describing the structural relationship between the "third plurality of discontinuities" and the other parts of the mat, and therefore, one skilled in the art could not make and/or use the invention. Applicant has amended claim 1 to remove the recitation of the "third plurality of discontinuities". In light of this amendment, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of this rejection.

Claims 1-11 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as being indefinite. The Office Action urges that it is unclear what is meant by the phrase a third plurality of discontinuities "corresponding" to the first plurality of discontinuities. The Office Action further states that the structural relationship between the third plurality of discontinuities and the first plurality of discontinuities is not clear and therefore the scope of the claims is indefinite. Applicant has amended claim 1 to remove the recitation of the "third plurality of discontinuities corresponding to the first plurality of discontinuities". In light of this amendment, Applicant respectfully requests withdrawal of this rejection.

Pending claim 1 recites "a first portion including a first conductive layer contacting a first non-conductive layer, wherein the first conductive layer and the first non-conductive layer define a first set of channels defining a first plurality of conductive strips oriented in a first direction, wherein the first portion includes first and second sides, wherein the first set of channels extend to first and second sides."

These limitations are supported by the originally filed specification. See, e.g., [0052] ("The pressure sensing mat 100 may include a first portion 102 and a second portion 104. An insulative layer 126 may be disposed between the first portion 102 and the second portion 104. As shown in FIG. 6, the first portion 102 may include a first conductive layer 106 that may be sandwiched between a first non-conductive layer 108 and a second non-conductive layer 110. The first non- conductive layer 108 and the first conductive layer 106 may define a first set of channels 112."); [0091] ("first set of channels 112 ... form the third conductive strip 130"); and Figure 7A (reproduced and annotated below).

The art of record does not disclose "the first set of channels extend to the first and second sides", as recited in claim 1. US 2013/0317393 ("Weiss") discloses other material layer 240a and layer of conductive layer 220a as depicted in Figure 3a. These layers do not define a first set of channels extending from first and second sides as recited in claim 1 because material layer 240a does not include any channel portions. US 2017/0010746 ("Hotelling") does not cure the defective teachings of Weiss. Hotelling is silent on the claimed extending channels. For at least these
reasons, independent claim 1 is patentable over the art of record. Claims 2-11 that depend on claim
1 are patentable for the at least the same reasons.
The Office Action indicates that claims 12-27 are allowed. Applicant notes with appreciation the allowance of claims 12-27.

Applicants do not acquiesce in the Examiner's characterizations of the art. For brevity and to advance prosecution, Applicants may not have addressed all characterizations of the art and reserve the right to do so in the course of further prosecution of this or a subsequent application. The absence of an explicit response by Applicants to any of the Examiner's positions does not constitute a concession to the examiner's positions. The fact that Applicants' comments have focused on particular arguments does not constitute a concession that there are no other arguments for patentability of the claims. Applicants submit that all of the dependent claims are patentable for at least the reasons given with respect to the claims on which they depend, as well as for their own specific limitations.

In view of the foregoing, the pending independent claims patentably define the present invention over the citations of record. Moreover, the dependent claims should be allowable for the same reasons as their respective base claims and further due to the additional features that they recite. Separate and individual consideration of the dependent claims is respectfully requested.

Applicant has made a genuine effort to respond to each of the Examiner's objections and rejections in advancing the prosecution of this case. Applicant believes that all formal and substantive requirements for patentability have been met and that the pending claims are in condition for allowance. A notice to this effect is respectfully requested. If the Examiner believes that additional issues remain, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned to expedite their resolution.
The Commissioner is hereby authorized to charge any fees or credit any overpayments as a result of the filing of this paper to our Deposit Account No. 02-3978.
